headline: Closings and new contracts slowed in October while listings kept climbing
summary: Across nine Middle Tennessee counties, 2,540 homes closed in October, 12% fewer than a year earlier, and pending sales fell 21% to 1,805.
15,379 homes were for sale, about six months of supply at the current pace, according to Greater Nashville Realtors.
Williamson County had 1,665 active listings in October, up 18.6% from a year earlier; Davidson County had 4,621, up 11.1%.
The nine-county median sale price was $499,990, and the median condo price was $343,776.

regional.title: The regional market (Greater Nashville Realtors, October 2026)
regional.note: Greater Nashville Realtors monthly housing snapshot, nine counties: Cheatham, Davidson, Dickson, Maury, Robertson, Rutherford, Sumner, Williamson and Wilson. All price ranges. Earlier editions used Realtracs' 27-county figures, so these numbers are not directly comparable with last month's regional table. GNR did not publish year-over-year changes for inventory or prices.

luxury.title: The luxury market
paragraphs: No October count of $1M+ closings or listings had been published when this edition was prepared, so this month leans on county listing data. Williamson County is a reasonable stand-in for the luxury tier: its median listing price was about $1.16M in September, so roughly half of its listings are priced above $1.1M. Williamson had 1,665 active listings in October, up 18.6% from a year earlier, and has held above 1,650 every month since July.

Across the nine-county region, pending sales fell 21% from a year earlier, a sharper drop than closings (down 12%). Contracts signed now become closings over the next month or two, so closings are likely to stay soft into the end of the year. With about six months of supply overall, buyers have more room to negotiate than they did a year ago, and sellers are competing with more listings.

neighborhoods.title: Luxury neighborhood medians
neighborhoods.note: Three months ending October 2026, all home types, from Redfin calculations of MLS and public-record data (retrieved November 18, 2026). Days on market is Redfin’s reported average. Forest Hills, Oak Hill, Thompson’s Station and Nolensville are the cities of those names; College Grove is ZIP 37046 and East Nashville is ZIP 37206. Belle Meade, Forest Hills and Oak Hill have few sales a month, so their figures can swing widely.

buyers: Six months of supply and a 21% drop in contracts give you room to negotiate on price, repairs and closing costs.
Ask how long a home has been listed and whether the price has been cut; the longer it has sat, the more room there usually is.
Well-priced homes in the most sought-after locations still sell, so have your financing ready before you tour.
sellers: Price to recent closed sales, not to what neighbors listed for in the spring.
With more listings to choose from, condition and presentation decide which homes get the showings.
If you can wait, a private pre-market launch lets you test the price before the home goes public.
